title: Source-isomorphism and signed-shift transport of the internal-Hom colimit comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe, with $\mathcal O$ commutative [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix the functorial K-injective target models for $H(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models]. For any small filtered diagram $N:I\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], put $N_\infty=\varinjlim_iN_i$ termwise and let $\alpha_A:\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i)\to H(A,N_\infty)$ be the image in $D(\mathcal M)$ of the canonical complex cocone map on these models. All colimits here are termwise sheaf colimits. The comparison is independent, up to the canonical identifications, of the complex representative of $A$. For every source isomorphism $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ the precomposition isomorphisms satisfy
$$H(e,N_\infty)\circ\alpha_{A'}=\alpha_A\circ\varinjlim_i H(e,N_i).$$
For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, let $s_{A,n,N}:H(A[n],N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(A,N)[-n]$ be the signed source-shift comparison, with cochain convention $K[n]^q=K^{q+n}$ and $d_{K[n]}=(-1)^n d_K$: on the Hom-complex models, for a complex $\mathcal L$ representing $A$ and the fixed K-injective model $\mathcal I$ of $N$, it is the chain isomorphism which reindexes $\prod_p\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L^{p+n},\mathcal I^{p+q})=\prod_{p'}\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L^{p'},\mathcal I^{p'+q-n})$ and multiplies degree-$q$ components by $(-1)^{nq}$; its sign depends only on $n,q$, not on $N$ (any normalization differing from it by a sign depending only on $n$ gives the same assertions). Let
$$t:\varinjlim_iH(A[n],N_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}(\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i))[-n]$$
be induced by the $s_{A,n,N_i}$ and the termwise colimit-shift identification. Then
$$s_{A,n,N_\infty}\circ\alpha_{A[n]}=\alpha_A[-n]\circ t.$$
These squares are natural in the target diagram. In particular their horizontal maps are conjugate by isomorphisms. No continuity or boundedness hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $N$.

proof.text: Use Grothendieck abelianness at independent site universes from the fixed functorial K-injective resolution theorem. For an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of filtered complex diagrams, apply the homology-colimit natural isomorphism in each integer degree. The colimit of the resulting natural isomorphism is invertible. Thus the induced termwise colimit map is a quasi-isomorphism, with no boundedness assumption.

proof.text: Extract the signed ordinary Hom shift components from the existing unique source-shift normalization. The product-projection formula LeftFormula proves their naturality jointly in both complex variables: project the two composites, use homComplexFunctor_map_f_pi, and commute the common scalar with composition. Descend this bifunctor shift using the actual localization factorization. Its ordinary-to-derived augmentation formula proves LeftNormalization, including arbitrary source representative isomorphisms. Uniqueness identifies the descended shift with the existing sourceShift; the factorization also gives its exact fixed-resolution formula.

proof.text: Whisker the signed ordinary chain isomorphism by the fixed target resolution and take its colimit. Compose with preservesColimitIso for the complex shift and the shift comparison of Q. This gives a natural isomorphism for strictColimit. Lift it uniquely through the source localization using rho and Q.commShiftIso; its representative formula is exactly the final chain-level identity of the theorem, before any test on derived injections. For the comparison square, test the chain-level equality on the colimit injections, then apply Q and the fixed-resolution formula of the normalized derived shift. Localization faithfulness extends the square to every derived source.

Evaluate the localized shift square at a diagram, use the identification with sourceShift, and package G, rho, alpha and the component shift isomorphisms. Their inverse maps exist by construction, so the horizontal comparison maps are conjugate. Filteredness was used only in the quasi-isomorphism argument of step 2.

Step 2: the homology-preserves-exact-colimits node applies because Mod(O) is Grothendieck with exact filtered colimits, so termwise colimits preserve quasi-isos. Step 6 injection test: s a_{L[n]} iota_i = B_L(u_i)[-n] s_i = a_L[-n] t iota_i, then Q commutes with shifts. Step 7: target naturality and the conjugation formulas.
